findings.claim: The observed window is the score-clock interval [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing, and the coordinate representation is native model endpoint world coordinates; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so no absolute affinity label is available in this evidence.

Continuous contrast functions over the complete observed support are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with a strong sign conflict and a large first-rate to last-rate reversal, and landmark_00_local_dx shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts; no polynomial fit was accepted and extrapolation is disallowed, so a constant rule is not supported and only observed-node interpolation is admissible.

Several landmark local contrast features have large early-window rate magnitudes that reverse sign by the last observed node (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z strongly negative, last_rate_z positive; landmark_00_local_cyy similar reversal), indicating time-conditioned rather than constant contrast behavior within the observed window.

Branch-adjusted raw-covariance effects for global centroid coordinates are null (all CIs spanning zero, q well above 0.05, same-sign batch fractions near chance), so centroid translation is not supported as a signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrast.

Shape covariance features show weak, mostly negative whole-window means with same-sign batch fractions around 0.79 for shape_xx and shape_yy, but only shape_yy reaches nominal p<0.05 and none survives multiplicity adjustment (q>0.15), so these are at most weak candidate contrasts, not established effects.

hypotheses.falsifier: If a constant rule matches the observed-node contrast as well as the time-conditioned rule (no rate sign change reproduced), the hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dy and landmark_00_local_cyy contrast values at observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates, 14 independent batches
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast on landmark local displacement features (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy / landmark_00_local_cyy) tracks the observed-node contrast better than a constant whole-window rule, because the observed rate changes sign within the window.

hypotheses.direction: negative shape-covariance contrast, no centroid contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: If shape-covariance effects lose their same-sign batch consistency or centroid effects become significant after multiplicity adjustment, the hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.observable: branch-adjusted raw covariance of shape_xx and shape_yy versus global_centroid_x/y/z
hypotheses.statement: Signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts are better expressed on shape-covariance features than on global centroid translation, since centroid raw-covariance effects are null while shape_xx/shape_yy show consistent negative same-sign batch fractions.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes are supplied; last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-selection versus descendant-survival comparison is unavailable.

No joint-diagnostic, turnover-accounting, increment-effect, endpoint-effect, survival-effect or lineage-support rows were read in this turn, so coupling/redundancy, parent-child increment versus cohort-composition, and ancestral-coverage/survivor-bias questions remain unaddressed.
Contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies; no causal neural-module or atom-velocity claim is supported.
Temperatures are immutable fixed parameters and were not evaluated as design variables.
